themes_detail.label: Street noise surge this week
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints spiked to 62 this week, a 401% increase over the 12.4 weekly average from the prior 8 weeks, suggesting a sudden environmental or construction-related disruption in the district.
evidence: 62 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 12.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.88)
401% spike represents statistically significant anomaly meeting high-severity threshold
Concentrated in single week suggests acute event rather than chronic issue
reporting_angles: Canvass residents along major corridors (Grand Concourse, Webster Ave, University Ave) to identify source: construction, street events, or infrastructure work
Check DOB permits and NYC Events calendar for major projects or permitted activities filed or approved this week
Interview Community Board 7 about whether they've fielded complaints or been notified of authorized work

themes_detail.label: Dangling street signs hazard
themes_detail.summary: Street sign dangling complaints jumped to 3 this week, a 1100% spike over the 0.2 weekly average, creating a public safety concern across the district.
evidence: 3 dangling street sign complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 6.35)
1100% spike indicates possible pattern of infrastructure neglect or storm damage
Safety hazard to pedestrians, particularly in high-traffic areas
reporting_angles: Obtain 311 complaint addresses to geolocate problem zones and visit sites for photo documentation
Contact NYC DOT to ask if they've identified systemic sign failure or if this reflects delayed maintenance
Check weather data for week prior to see if storm or wind event triggered deterioration

themes_detail.label: Garbage disposal complaints spike
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints jumped to 9 this week, a 454% increase over the 1.6 weekly average, suggesting a localized sanitation or building code enforcement issue.
evidence: 9 residential disposal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.6)
454% spike indicates concentrated problem, likely building-specific or neighborhood-specific
May reflect failure of building waste management or unauthorized dumping
reporting_angles: Obtain 311 complaint addresses to identify if complaints cluster in specific buildings or blocks
Interview affected residents about whether they're experiencing overflow, non-collection, or building-level neglect
Contact NYC Sanitation to ask if there are route delays, service suspensions, or enforcement actions this week

themes_detail.label: Park noise complaints spike
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints spiked to 3 complaints 3 weeks ago (a 2300% increase over the 0.1 weekly baseline), signaling a new or persistent activity pattern in district parks.
evidence: 3 park noise complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 8.69)
2300% spike indicates sudden onset of park-based noise activity
Volume is modest but statistical anomaly suggests change in park usage or events
reporting_angles: Obtain 311 complaint addresses to identify which parks are affected (Bronx Park, Van Cortlandt Park edges, or smaller neighborhood parks)
Check NYC Parks calendar for permitted events, concerts, or athletic tournaments scheduled 3 weeks ago
Visit parks to observe current use patterns and interview Parks enforcement about noise complaints and permitting

themes_detail.label: Overgrown trees and branches hazard
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints spiked to 3 complaints 2 weeks ago, a 2300% increase over the 0.1 weekly baseline, indicating possible deferred maintenance across the district's street tree inventory.
evidence: 3 overgrown tree complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 8.69)
2300% spike suggests sudden awareness or emergence of deferred tree maintenance
Potential safety hazard to pedestrians and vehicles; also signals wider infrastructure maintenance gaps
reporting_angles: Obtain 311 complaint addresses to map problem areas and identify tree species and locations
Contact NYC Parks forestry division to ask about pruning schedules, crew capacity, and backlog in CD 207
Report on whether community board budget requests (which repeatedly ask for tree and environmental funding) correlate with these complaints
